questions.q: What does transaction feed code mapping accomplish in a corporate card program?
options: It maps a merchant's category code to the correct expense type automatically
It sets each employee's salary
It determines the company's fiscal year
It permanently blocks all card transactions over $10
questions.explain: Feed code mapping translates the merchant category code from the card issuer into the matching Castellan expense type, like 'restaurants' to Business Meal.

questions.q: What happens to a corporate card transaction the moment it arrives from the card issuer's feed?
options: It immediately posts to the General Ledger
It immediately reimburses the employee
It lands as an unassigned card transaction that the employee must review and attach to a report
It is automatically deleted after 24 hours
questions.explain: Transactions arrive as unassigned items in a queue; nothing posts to the ledger or gets reimbursed until the employee attaches it to a submitted expense report.

questions.q: On an individual-liability corporate card, who does Payables actually pay once the expense report is approved?
options: The card issuer directly
The employee, who is personally responsible for paying their own card bill
No one; individual-liability cards are never reimbursed
The employee's manager
questions.explain: On an individual-liability card, the employee personally owes the issuer, so Payables reimburses the employee after approval.

questions.q: On a company-liability corporate card, who does Payables pay once the expense report is approved?
options: The card issuer directly, since the company itself is responsible for the balance
The employee, the same as an individual-liability card
Nobody is ever paid on a company-liability card
The employee's spouse
questions.explain: On a company-liability card, Castellan itself owes the balance, so Payables pays the card issuer directly and the employee is not reimbursed for that line.

questions.q: Why is a card transaction that sits unassigned for 30+ days a real operational problem?
options: It isn't a problem; unassigned transactions have no consequences
It represents a liability with no accounting entry and no business justification on file
It automatically triggers a tax audit by the government
It causes the General Ledger to shut down entirely
questions.explain: An old unassigned transaction means money the company may owe has no accounting record or justification, which is why audit rules flag aging transactions and escalate to managers.
